clue.text: Joky item of music men put on centuries ago

parts.note: cod as an adjective means mock or jokey, as in a cod accent
a piece is an item of music, a composition

explanation.surface: A humorous number that male musicians performed long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joky item of music' reads as one phrase, but 'Joky' stands alone: cod is British slang for mock, as in a cod accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A codpiece was a pouch worn by men over the front of breeches in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.

clue.text: Sailors cheered

definitions.meaning: crowed, exulted: an old past tense of crow is ..., as in 'the cock ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Crew is both a noun for a ship's sailors and an archaic past tense of crow, to cheer exultantly.

clue.text: Rest after death — whence one heads heavenwards?

indicators.note: after places the word for rest behind the word for death in the answer

parts.note: departure is a euphemism for death, a departing this life
to lounge is to rest or laze

explanation.surface: A meditation on resting after dying, and where souls set off for heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests souls rising to heaven; the definition really means the airport room from which passengers take off into the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Airline passengers wait in this airport room before their flights climb into the skies.

clue.text: Romantic bit of business is contained in it

indicators.note: contained in puts the business word together with is inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
a deal is a piece of business, a transaction
taken as written

explanation.surface: A romantic touch in a business transaction is kept within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic, as a noun, is a dreamer who pursues ideals rather than practical realities.

clue.text: Rise of Conservative Member

parts.note: a limb, an arm or leg, is a member of the body

explanation.surface: The ascent of a Tory Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an ascent or rise, whether up a hill or in rank.

clue.text: This newspaper has dumped me for a nymph

indicators.note: has dumped says the following word is thrown out of the newspaper's name

parts.note: the clue appears in The Times, so this newspaper is the Times
taken as written

explanation.surface: The paper has dropped the writer in favour of a nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: Thetis was a sea nymph in Greek myth, the mother of Achilles.

clue.text: Divine witch takes no end of care about familiar

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word goes round the familiar
no end of means the final letter of the word for care is dropped

parts.note: heed means attention or care
a witch's familiar is traditionally a cat

explanation.surface: A holy witch looks after her familiar with endless care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link. 'no end of' trims the last letter from the synonym before it goes round the familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate was the Greek goddess associated with witchcraft and magic, so a divine figure of witchery.

clue.text: Contest ending in defeat -— falling short, faltering

clue.text: Film music was tedious to hear? It should feature up-to date numbers

definitions.text: It should feature up-to date numbers

parts.note: a film's score is its music

indicators.note: to hear says the word for being tiresome is said aloud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: something tedious bored its audience

explanation.surface: A complaint that a soundtrack was dull, followed by a hint about current figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreboard at a game displays the current score, figures updated as play goes on.

clue.text: Change country of residence good to move into Muslim state

indicators.note: to move into says the letter for good goes inside the state

parts.note: an emirate is a state ruled by an emir, as in the Gulf

explanation.surface: Advice on going to live in an Islamic country.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's own country and settle in another.

clue.text: A bit of indirect speech? That's. nicer to hear

definitions.text: A bit of indirect speech? That's. nicer to hear

parts.words: A bit of indirect speech? That's. nicer to hear
parts.note: a mild, roundabout expression chosen so that something unpleasant sounds kinder, such as 'passed away'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Indirect speech' suggests the grammar term reported speech; here it means a roundabout way of putting something. The stray full stop is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle word substituted for a harsh or blunt one, so that the listener finds it more palatable.

clue.text: Broadcast probing firm's capital

indicators.note: probing means the broadcast word pushes inside the firm

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A television programme investigates a company's headquarters city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Examination of ethics offering no end of altruism

indicators.note: offering no says a letter is left out of the ethics word

parts.note: moral means concerning ethics

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A test of ethical understanding that leaves out selflessness.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of 'altruism' is M, which is removed from MORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a language test.

clue.text: Number 'of spectators admitted to dance company briefly see no serious work

indicators.note: admitted to puts the crowd figure inside the shortened dance company
briefly means the last letter of the company word is cut

parts.note: a ballet is a company of dancers
the gate is the number of people attending a match

explanation.surface: Spectators let in to see a ballet troupe watch something light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link, and 'briefly' trims the company's last letter. The apostrophe before 'of' is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a trifle, and in music a short light piece: nothing weighty.

clue.text: Cooked meat and whisky that Cooperative had plenty of?

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of meat are rearranged, as food is altered by cooking

parts.note: whisky is a spirit, a distilled drink

explanation.surface: A meal and a drink of the kind a cooperative stocked in quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges MEAT to TEAM. 'Cooperative' looks like a shop name but describes a person who works well with others.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cooperative shows willingness to pull together with a group, which is the essence of collective morale.

clue.text: Energy given to search organised to capture one horseman

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
a quest is a search

indicators.note: to capture means the word for organised holds the numeral one

parts.note: to run something is to organise it, so ran
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hunt was set up, with a burst of energy, to catch a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrian is a person who rides horses, especially skilfully.

clue.text: By the way, this is a useful source of information

definitions.text: By the way, this is a useful source of information

parts.words: By the way, this is a useful source of information
parts.note: 'by the way' read literally means beside the road: a roadside board that tells travellers directions

explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' looks like a casual aside but means literally positioned along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside board giving drivers directions or warnings sits by the road to inform them.

clue.text: Some returned for facial and haircut

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone came back for a facial and a new hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'and haircut' as the definition; 'and' is a link, so the definition is 'haircut' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a hairstyle of tight curls shaped into a round mass.

clue.text: Harangue one third of beaten political party

indicators.note: one third of takes the first two of the six letters of beaten

parts.note: Labour is one of the main UK political parties

explanation.surface: Lambasting a political party that lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour someone is to attack them at length with words, to harangue.

clue.text: Sporting encounter gutted male entrant

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed from both words, leaving their first and last letters

explanation.surface: A competitor at a sporting event was dismayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like British slang for upset, but it strips each word to its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A meet is a sporting gathering, such as an athletics competition.

clue.text: Beginning to point, excellent hunting dog, foremost in the field

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: ace means excellent
a setter is a gun dog used in hunting

explanation.surface: A fine pointer and setter lead the hunt across the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' and 'hunting dog' suggest a pointer, but only P is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter is the leader who sets the speed others follow.

clue.text: Be less' strict about fast

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Being less rigid about fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe after 'less' is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften one's attitude, to become less severe.

clue.text: Academic's about to replace his, fine computer unit

indicators.note: to replace says one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: a professor is an academic
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A professor is about to swap his fine computer part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' is a link; the stray comma is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The processor is the central chip of a computer that carries out instructions.

clue.text: Stupid talk about a Sunday joint

indicators.note: about means the word for nonsense goes around the other letters

parts.note: rot is nonsense, stupid talk

explanation.surface: Foolish chatter about a Sunday roast dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunday joint' reads as one phrase, but Sunday gives S and the definition is 'joint'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat cooked in the oven, traditional for Sunday lunch in Britain.

clue.text: Copy Times -— it's the high-point

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Imitating The Times newspaper is the peak of achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex of something is its highest point or peak.

clue.text: Picture vessels being overturned

indicators.note: being overturned in a down clue means the word for vessels is read upwards

parts.note: pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: An image of boats capsizing.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a snapshot, a casual photograph.

clue.text: Where to cook a spread?

definitions.meaning: a kitchen stove with an oven and hotplates

explanation.definitionFit: Range names both a large cooking stove and a scope or spread of values.

clue.text: Glitzy newspaper, say, in part of Wales

parts.note: glam, short for glamorous, means glitzy
a newspaper is an example of an organ, a medium of communication

explanation.surface: A showy newspaper in a Welsh region.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorgan is a historic county in south Wales.

clue.text: Attempt to limit trouble, coming to agreement

indicators.note: to limit means the attempt word encloses the trouble word

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to eat someone is to trouble them, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: An effort to contain unrest, leading to a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.

clue.text: Big-name actor's trendy — one in SF movie?

parts.note: a star is a big-name actor; with the possessive it gives stars
hip means trendy, fashionable

explanation.surface: A famous actor is cool, perhaps someone appearing in a science-fiction film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in SF movie?' suggests a cast member, but it means a spacecraft; SF is science fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacecraft that travel between stars are a staple of science-fiction films.
